terms.definition: The explosion of a massive star when its iron core collapses and rebounds — for weeks it outshines its entire galaxy.
terms.function: The death event of stars above about eight solar masses.

terms.definition: The end-product center of a massive star: iron is the element that takes energy to fuse, so once it forms, fusion stops releasing energy and gravity takes over.
terms.whereItIs: The center of the pre-explosion star
terms.whyItMatters: The moment the iron core forms is the fuse for the whole explosion.

terms.definition: The bounce that tears a supernova apart — the collapsing core stops abruptly and throws a pressure wave outward at close to light speed.
terms.function: Carries the explosion energy outward through the star's layers.

terms.definition: The expanding shell of debris left after the explosion, glowing for thousands of years as it cools and mixes with the surrounding gas.
terms.whereItIs: The outward-moving shell around the new neutron star or black hole
terms.whyItMatters: It delivers newly made heavy elements into the galaxy.

terms.definition: The forging of elements during the explosion — extreme heat and fast neutron captures build everything heavier than iron, from silver to uranium.
terms.function: Produces most of the heavy elements that make up the Earth and living things.
